full_judgment:
3. The High Court Division by the impugned Judgment made the Rule absolute directing the petitioners to "mutate the names of the petitioners (writ-petitioners) in respect of the land in record-of-right upon changing ownership/possession of the land" within three months observing that in view of the judgments of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 5380 of 1991 and writ petition No.4997 of 2008, the petitioners are under obligation to mutate the disputed property in favour of the writ-petitioners under sections 143 and 143(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Against the said judgment and order, the writ-respondent Nos. 1-4 preferred Civil Petition No. 1718 of 2010. One Samar Chakrabartee and 4 others who are not parties in the writ petition preferred Civil Petition No. 869 of 2011 against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that they instituted Other Class Suit No. 197 of 2011 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong seeking declaration that the deed dated 11th February, 2009 is forged, collusive and not binding upon them, that the writ-petitioners' predecessors AKM Bashir Ahmed and others executed a collusive agreement with the writ-petitioners and that the writ-respondents obtained a collusive decree. They claimed title and ownership of the disputed property by way of amicable partition; the BS Khatian was prepared behind their back, and the High Court Division without affording them any opportunity passed the impugned judgment which is not binding upon them. 

 10. The case considered by the High Court Division is quite distinguishable. In that case, Qazi Kamal with the prior permission of RAJUK purchased a plot of land with building at Gulshan from the original allotted after performing formalities and on payment of required fees as demanded by the RAJUK. Thereupon, the purchaser Qazi Kamal applied to the RAJUK for mutation of the plot with building by enclosing a copy of the deed. In the mean time, some inimical persons of the original lessee made a complaint to RAJUK alleging that he got allotment of the plot by filing a false affidavit. Pursuant to such complaint, RAJUK took a resolution not to mutate the said plot in favour of Qazi Kamal. In the context of the matter, Qazi Kamal filed a writ petition. This Division noticed that RAJUK had not taken any step to cancel the allotment of the original lessee, the vendor of Qazi Kamal or determined the lease of the vendor as per lease deed. In view of the above admitted position, this Division held that Qazi Kamal was not in any way connected with the filing of the alleged false affidavit by this vendor and that Qazi Kamal being a bonafide purchaser for value without notice to the act of this vendor, RAJUK acted illegally in denying the mutation. So, the High Court Division failed to appreciate the statement of law argued by this Division in the above case which has no manner of application in this case. 

 11. Writ petitioners did not enclose any paper or order of the Revenue Officer pursuant to the filing of their application for mutation other than an application said to have been made on 12th May, 2009 to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong. They stated that they prayed to the Assistant Commissioner (Lands, Sadar), Chittagong for mutation of their names who expressed his inability to mutate their names. They did not state when they applied for mutation and when the Assistant Commissioner (Lands) refused their prayer. 

 12. Since they claimed mutation of their names on the basis of the sale deed, section 143(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act will hold the field. The procedure for mutation of record-of-rights by way of transfer of a plot of land has been provided in chapter VI of the Tenancy Rules, 1954. Rule 23(3) of the said Rules provides that the Revenue Officer either on application or on receipt of a report of the Tahsildar shall make correction in the record-of-rights, after consulting with previous settlement records, Collector's copy of record-of-rights and Register II and making such other enquiries as he considers necessary. The Revenue Officer is required to see whether any entry has been procured by fraud while making any order for correction of an entry and his decision should be based on the report of the Tahsildar. The Revenue Officer shall carefully examine the report and unless he is satisfied with the correctness of the previous record-of-rights, he shall not make any order and in doing so, he is required to follow such procedures as may be directed by the Land Administration Board/the Board of Revenue. 

 13. Rule 24(4) provides that when the land vests in or comes to the possession of the Government, it shall be recorded in the khas khatian. Thus, there is no gainsaying fact that the mutation of record-of-rights requires enquiry, perusal of previous settlement records, collector's record and the annexed Register. These Rules show that the mutation of the record-of-rights is not mere routine work rather such mutation requires examination of the records which may take time. The writ-petitioners without awaiting the decision of the Revenue Officer moved the High Court Division by making a mere statement that the Revenue Officer refused their prayer.
